sanskrit: vālmīkinaivam uktas tu rāghavaḥ pratyabhāṣata prāñjalir jagato madhye dṛṣṭvā tāṃ devavarṇinīm
english: Thus addressed by Vālmīki, Rāghava replied with palms joined in the midst of the assembly, having beheld that one of divine complexion.

sanskrit: evam etan mahābhāga yathā vadasi dharmavit pratyayo hi mama brahmaṃs tava vākyair akalmaṣaiḥ
english: "So it is, O highly blessed one, O knower of dharma, exactly as you declare. I am convinced, O Brahman, by your words that are without blemish."

sanskrit: pratyayo hi purā datto vaidehyā surasaṃnidhau seyaṃ lokabhayād brahmann apāpety abhijānatā parityaktā mayā sītā tad bhavān kṣantum arhati
english: "Proof was indeed given formerly by Vaidehī in the presence of the gods. Yet knowing her to be without sin, I abandoned Sītā out of fear of what the world would say, O Brahman — may you forgive that."

sanskrit: jānāmi cemau putrau me yamajātau kuśīlavau śuddhāyāṃ jagato madhye maithilyāṃ prītir astu me
english: "And I know these two sons of mine, Kuśa and Lava, born as twins; may I now have the joy of being reunited with Maithilī, whose purity has been proclaimed in the midst of the world."

sanskrit: abhiprāyaṃ tu vijñāya rāmasya surasattamāḥ pitāmahaṃ puraskṛtya sarva eva samāgatāḥ
english: Understanding the intention of Rāma, the foremost of the gods, all of them assembled together with the Grandfather Brahmā at their head.

sanskrit: ādityā vasavo rudrā viśve deśā marudgaṇāḥ aśvināv ṛṣigandharvā apsarāṇāṃ gaṇās tathā sādhyāś ca devāḥ sarve te sarve ca paramarṣayaḥ
english: The Ādityas, Vasus, Rudras, Viśvedeva, troops of Maruts, the two Aśvins, the seers, the Gandharvas, the hosts of Apsarases, the Sādhya gods — all of them — and all the great seers came.

sanskrit: tato vāyuḥ śubhaḥ puṇyo divyagandho manoramaḥ taṃ janaughaṃ suraśreṣṭho hlādayām āsa sarvataḥ
english: Then an auspicious, holy, divinely fragrant, and delightful wind, the best of the celestials, gladdened that multitude of people on every side.

sanskrit: tad adbhutam ivācintyaṃ nirīkṣante samāhitāḥ mānavāḥ sarvarāṣṭrebhyaḥ pūrvaṃ kṛtayuge yathā
english: The people assembled from all the realms gazed upon that wondrous, inconceivable event with concentrated minds, as in the Kṛtayuga of old.

sanskrit: sarvān samāgatān dṛṣṭvā sītā kāṣāyavāsinī abravīt prāñjalir vākyam adhodṛṣṭir avānmukhī
english: Sītā, clad in an ochre robe, beholding all who had gathered, spoke words with palms joined, her gaze lowered and her face cast downward.

sanskrit: yathāhaṃ rāghavād anyaṃ manasāpi na cintaye tathā me mādhavī devī vivaraṃ dātum arhati
english: "As I have never even in mind thought of any man other than Rāghava, so may the goddess Mādhavī — the Earth — grant me an opening."

sanskrit: tathā śapantyāṃ vaidehyāṃ prādurāsīt tad adbhutam bhūtalād utthitaṃ divyaṃ siṃhāsanam anuttamam
english: As Vaidehī was thus taking this oath, that wonder appeared: from the surface of the earth rose a divine, incomparable throne.

sanskrit: dhriyamāṇaṃ śirobhis tan nāgair amitavikramaiḥ divyaṃ divyena vapuṣā sarvaratnavibhūṣitam
english: It was borne on the heads of serpents of immeasurable might, divine in its divine form, adorned with all kinds of jewels.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tu dharaṇī devī bāhubhyāṃ gṛhya maithilīm svāgatenābhinandyainām āsane copaveṣayat
english: And upon it the goddess Earth, taking Maithilī in her arms, welcomed her with a greeting and caused her to be seated on that throne.

sanskrit: tām āsanagatāṃ dṛṣṭvā praviśantīṃ rasātalam puṇyavṛṣṭir avicchinnā divyā sītām avākirat
english: Beholding her seated on the throne and descending into the netherworld, an unceasing shower of divine flowers rained down upon Sītā.

sanskrit: sādhukāraś ca sumahān devānāṃ sahasotthitaḥ sādhu sādhv iti vai sīte yasyās te śīlam īdṛśam
english: A very great cry of "bravo!" arose at once from the gods: "Bravo, bravo, O Sītā, whose virtue is of such a nature!"

sanskrit: evaṃ bahuvidhā vāco hy antarikṣagatāḥ surāḥ vyājahrur hṛṣṭamanaso dṛṣṭvā sītāpraveśanam
english: In this manner the gods who were stationed in the sky uttered many such words with joyful minds, having witnessed the descent of Sītā.

sanskrit: yajñavāṭagatāś cāpi munayaḥ sarva eva te rājānaś ca naravyāghrā vismayān noparemire
english: And the sages who had gathered at the sacrificial enclosure, as well as the kings, those tigers among men, could not cease from their amazement.

sanskrit: antarikṣe ca bhūmau ca sarve sthāvarajaṅgamāḥ dānavāś ca mahākāyāḥ pātāle pannagādhipāḥ
english: In the sky and on the earth, all beings, both stationary and moving, the great-bodied Dānavas, the lords of serpents in the underworld —

sanskrit: ke cid vineduḥ saṃhṛṣṭāḥ ke cid dhyānaparāyaṇāḥ ke cid rāmaṃ nirīkṣante ke cit sītām acetanāḥ
english: — some cried out in great joy, some were absorbed in meditation, some gazed at Rāma, some were rendered senseless gazing at Sītā.

sanskrit: sītāpraveśanaṃ dṛṣṭvā teṣām āsīt samāgamaḥ taṃ muhūrtam ivātyarthaṃ sarvaṃ saṃmohitaṃ jagat
english: At the sight of Sītā's descent, there was a great gathering of those beings; and at that moment the entire world was utterly overwhelmed.

sanskrit: tadāvasāne yajñasya rāmaḥ paramadurmanāḥ apaśyamāno vaidehīṃ mene śūnyam idaṃ jagat śokena paramāyatto na śāntiṃ manasāgamat
english: At the conclusion of that sacrifice, Rāma, deeply grief-stricken, seeing Vaidehī no more, considered this world empty. Overcome utterly by sorrow, he could find no peace of mind.

sanskrit: visṛjya pārthivān sarvān ṛkṣavānararākṣasān janaughaṃ brahmamukhyānāṃ vittapūrṇaṃ vyasarjayat
english: He dismissed all the kings, the bears, monkeys, and rākṣasas, and sent away the assembled throng of Brahman-led seers, richly laden with gifts.

sanskrit: tato visṛjya tān sarvān rāmo rājīvalocanaḥ hṛdi kṛtvā tadā sītām ayodhyāṃ praviveśa saḥ
english: Having dismissed them all, Rāma, the lotus-eyed, then entered Ayodhyā carrying Sītā in his heart.

sanskrit: na sītāyāḥ parāṃ bhāryāṃ vavre sa raghunandanaḥ yajñe yajñe ca patnyarthaṃ jānakī kāñcanī bhavat
english: That scion of Raghu took no other wife beyond Sītā; at every sacrifice a golden image of Jānakī served as the ritual consort.

sanskrit: daśavarṣasahasrāṇi vājimedham upākarot vājapeyān daśaguṇāṃs tathā bahusuvarṇakān
english: For ten thousand years he performed the Aśvamedha sacrifice, and Vājapeya sacrifices ten times that number, together with many sacrifices endowed with great gold.

sanskrit: agniṣṭomātirātrābhyāṃ gosavaiś ca mahādhanaiḥ īje kratubhir anyaiś ca sa śrīmān āptadakṣiṇaiḥ
english: That glorious one performed also the Agniṣṭoma, the Atirātra, the Gosava with great wealth, and other rites in which the sacrificial fees were duly rendered.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa kālaḥ sumahān rājyasthasya mahātmanaḥ dharme prayatamānasya vyatīyād rāghavasya tu
english: In this manner a very great span of time passed for Rāghava, the great-souled one, who was established in his kingdom and who strove ever in the path of dharma.

sanskrit: ṛkṣavānararakṣāṃsi sthitā rāmasya śāsane anurajyanti rājāno ahany ahani rāghavam
english: The bears, monkeys, and rākṣasas remained under Rāma's authority; the kings were attached to Rāghava day by day.

sanskrit: kāle varṣati parjanyaḥ subhikṣaṃ vimalā diśaḥ hṛṣṭapuṣṭajanākīrṇaṃ puraṃ janapadas tathā
english: Rain fell in season, abundance prevailed, the directions were clear; the city and the countryside were filled with people who were joyful and well-nourished.

sanskrit: nākāle mriyate kaś cin na vyādhiḥ prāṇināṃ tadā nādharmaś cābhavat kaś cid rāme rājyaṃ praśāsati
english: No one died before his time, no disease afflicted living beings, and there was no adharma whatsoever while Rāma was governing the kingdom.

sanskrit: atha dīrghasya kālasya rāmamātā yaśasvinī putrapautraiḥ parivṛtā kāladharmam upāgamat
english: Then, after a long time, Rāma's illustrious mother, surrounded by her sons and grandsons, attained the fate decreed by time — she died.

sanskrit: anviyāya sumitrāpi kaikeyī ca yaśasvinī dharmaṃ kṛtvā bahuvidhaṃ tridive paryavasthitā
english: Sumitrā also followed, and the illustrious Kaikeyī; having performed dharma in its many forms, they were established in the three heavens.

sanskrit: sarvāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ svarge rājñā daśarathena ca samāgatā mahābhāgāḥ saha dharmaṃ ca lebhire
english: All of them were established in heaven and were reunited with King Daśaratha, those highly blessed ones together attained dharma.

sanskrit: tāsāṃ rāmo mahādānaṃ kāle kāle prayacchati mātṝṇām aviśeṣeṇa brāhmaṇeṣu tapasviṣu
english: Rāma made great offerings for them in due seasons, for his mothers without distinction, among Brāhmaṇas and ascetics.

sanskrit: pitryāṇi bahuratnāni yajñān paramadustarān cakāra rāmo dharmātmā pitṝn devān vivardhayan
english: Rāma, whose soul was established in dharma, performed ancestral rites with many jewels and sacrifices of the utmost magnificence, thereby honoring the ancestors and the gods.

sanskrit: kasya cit tv atha kālasya yudhājit kekayo nṛpaḥ svaguruṃ preṣayām āsa rāghavāya mahātmane
english: Now after some time, Yudhājit, king of the Kekayas, sent his own preceptor to the great-souled Rāghava.

sanskrit: gārgyam aṅgirasaḥ putraṃ brahmarṣim amitaprabham daśa cāśvasahasrāṇi prītidānam anuttamam
english: He sent the brahmarṣi Gārgya, son of Aṅgiras, of immeasurable splendor, and ten thousand horses as an incomparable gift of affection.

sanskrit: kambalāni ca ratnāni citravastram athottamam rāmāya pradadau rājā bahūny ābharaṇāni ca
english: The king presented to Rāma also blankets, jewels, choice embroidered garments, and many ornaments.

sanskrit: śrutvā tu rāghavo gārgyaṃ maharṣiṃ samupāgatam mātulasyāśvapatinaḥ priyaṃ dūtam upāgatam
english: Hearing that the great seer Gārgya had arrived — the beloved envoy of his maternal uncle Aśvapati —

sanskrit: pratyudgamya ca kākutsthaḥ krośamātraṃ sahānugaḥ gārgyaṃ saṃpūjayām āsa dhanaṃ tat pratigṛhya ca
english: — Kākutstha went out to meet him, accompanied by his retinue, to a distance of a krośa, and honored Gārgya, receiving that wealth.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭvā ca prītidaṃ sarvaṃ kuśalaṃ mātulasya ca upaviṣṭaṃ mahābhāgaṃ rāmaḥ praṣṭuṃ pracakrame
english: Having asked in a pleasing manner after the welfare of his maternal uncle, Rāma began to question the highly blessed one when he was seated.

sanskrit: kim āha matulo vākyaṃ yadarthaṃ bhagavān iha prāpto vākyavidāṃ śreṣṭha sākṣād iva bṛhaspatiḥ
english: "What message does my maternal uncle convey? For what purpose has the blessed one come here, O best among those versed in speech, like Bṛhaspati himself in person?"

sanskrit: rāmasya bhāṣitaṃ śrutvā brahmarṣiḥ kāryavistaram vaktum adbhutasaṃkāśaṃ rāghavāyopacakrame
english: Hearing the words of Rāma, the brahmarṣi, wondrous in appearance, began to narrate to Rāghava the full details of the matter.

sanskrit: mātulas te mahābāho vākyam āha nararṣabha yudhājit prītisaṃyuktaṃ śrūyatāṃ yadi rocate
english: "Your maternal uncle Yudhājit speaks this message, O mighty-armed one, O bull among men — may it please you to hear it, full of affection."

sanskrit: ayaṃ gandharvaviṣayaḥ phalamūlopaśobhitaḥ sindhor ubhayataḥ pārśve deśaḥ paramaśobhanaḥ
english: "This Gandharva territory, adorned with fruits and roots, a most beautiful region on both banks of the Sindhu —"

sanskrit: taṃ ca rakṣanti gandharvāḥ sāyudhā yuddhakovidāḥ śailūṣasya sutā vīrās tisraḥ koṭyo mahābalāḥ
english: "— it is guarded by Gandharvas, armed and skilled in battle, sons of Śailūṣa, thirty million heroes of great might."

sanskrit: tān vinirjitya kākutstha gandharvaviṣayaṃ śubham niveśaya mahābāho dve pure susamāhitaḥ
english: "Having conquered them, O Kākutstha, O mighty-armed one, please establish two well-ordered cities in that auspicious Gandharva territory."

sanskrit: anyasya na gatis tatra deśaś cāyaṃ suśobhanaḥ rocatāṃ te mahābāho nāhaṃ tvām anṛtaṃ vade
english: "No other man's path leads there; that region is supremely beautiful. May it please you, O mighty-armed one — I do not speak falsely to you."

sanskrit: tac chrutvā rāghavaḥ prīto maharṣer mātulasya ca uvāca bāḍham ity evaṃ bharataṃ cānvavaikṣata
english: Hearing this, Rāghava was pleased with the great seer and with his maternal uncle's message, and said "So be it," glancing then toward Bharata.

sanskrit: so 'bravīd rāghavaḥ prītaḥ prāñjalipragraho dvijam imau kumārau taṃ deśaṃ brahmarṣe vijayiṣyataḥ
english: The pleased Rāghava, with folded hands, said to the twice-born sage: "These two princes will conquer that territory, O brahmarṣi."

sanskrit: bharatasyātmajau vīrau takṣaḥ puṣkala eva ca mātulena suguptau tau dharmeṇa ca samāhitau
english: "The two heroic sons of Bharata — Takṣa and Puṣkala — well protected by their maternal uncle, and both intent on dharma."

sanskrit: bharataṃ cāgrataḥ kṛtvā kumārau sabalānugau nihatya gandharvasutān dve pure vibhajiṣyataḥ
english: "With Bharata going in front, the two princes, accompanied by their forces and retinue, will slay the sons of the Gandharvās and then divide between them the two cities."

sanskrit: niveśya te puravare ātmājau saṃniveśya ca āgamiṣyati me bhūyaḥ sakāśam atidhārmikaḥ
english: "Having established those two excellent cities and settled his own sons there, the most righteous Bharata will return once more to my side."

sanskrit: brahmarṣim evam uktvā tu bharataṃ sabalānugam ājñāpayām āsa tadā kumārau cābhyaṣecayat
english: Having spoken thus to the brahmarṣi, he then commanded Bharata along with his army and retinue, and consecrated the two princes.

sanskrit: nakṣatreṇa ca saumyena puraskṛtyāṅgiraḥ sutam bharataḥ saha sainyena kumārābhyāṃ ca niryayau
english: Under an auspicious lunar asterism, placing the son of Aṅgiras at their head, Bharata set forth with his army and with the two princes.

sanskrit: sā senā śakrayukteva naragān niryayāv atha rāghavānugatā dūraṃ durādharṣā surāsuraiḥ
english: That army, like Indra's own forces, marched out through the city gates, escorted far by Rāghava, and was formidable to gods and asuras alike.

sanskrit: māṃsāśīni ca sattvāni rakṣāṃsi sumahānti ca anujagmuś ca bharataṃ rudhirasya pipāsayā
english: Flesh-eating creatures and very great rākṣasas also followed Bharata, thirsting for blood.

sanskrit: bhūtagrāmāś ca bahavo māṃsabhakṣāḥ sudāruṇāḥ gandharvaputramāṃsāni bhoktukāmāḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: And many hosts of spirits, flesh-eating, exceedingly fierce, numbering in the thousands, desirous of feasting on the flesh of the Gandharva's sons, followed along.

sanskrit: siṃhavyāghrasṛgālānāṃ khecarāṇāṃ ca pakṣiṇām bahūni vai sahasrāṇi senāyā yayur agrataḥ
english: Many thousands of lions, tigers, and jackals, as well as birds of the air, went in front of the army.

sanskrit: adhyardhamāsam uṣitā pathi senā nirāmayā hṛṣṭapuṣṭajanākīrṇā kekayaṃ samupāgamat
english: The army, healthy and unimpeded, having spent a month and a half on the road, arrived at Kekaya, filled with men who were cheerful and well-provisioned.
